question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution:
The correct answer is **"keep out."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Keep out"** means to prevent someone or something from entering a particular place or area. (किसी व्यक्ति या चीज़ को किसी विशेष स्थान या क्षेत्र में प्रवेश करने से रोकना)

 
 
• **Example**: *The curtains help **keep out**__ the drafts.*
 
 
 
• It is the most appropriate option to fill in the blank as it fits the context of preventing something from entering.
 
• The correct answer is option 3.
 
• Correct passage:

His only __regret__ was that he had no rifle. While running away from the village below, he had forgotten the rifle in a hurry. An unpardonable __lapse__, but it was now too late to make amends for it. __Had__ he had the rifle, his pursuers would not have dared follow him with such brazen confidence. He would have hidden behind a rock and waited for them. As they came within his rifle’s range, he would have picked them off one by one. But now he could do__ nothing__ about it. He was unarmed. But come what may, he must __**keep out**__ of their rifle’s range.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1, "keep from"**, means to refrain from doing something or to prevent someone from doing something. (कुछ करने से रोकना या किसी को कुछ करने से रोकना)
 
• **Option 2, "keep within"**, means to stay within certain limits or boundaries. (कुछ सीमाओं या सीमाओं के भीतर रहना)
 
• **Option 4, "keep of"**, is not a correct English phrase.
